title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 683-685 of the 'suite à La Longue Marche'). Grothendieck is building group schemes over Spec Z. They describe pairs of 'twists' of the two torsion generators ρ (order 3 type) and σ (order 2/4 type), which act on a rank-2 lattice M with basis λ0, λ1, together with a 'head' quotient M_0 and units O_12^*. They are linear or abelianised models of the automorphism groups Z_{ρ,σ} that appear on the next page: automorphisms u with u(ρ) conjugate to ξρ, u(σ) conjugate to ησ, plus an 'equation of heads'.

On the previous page he defined N^{0+} as the kernel of M×M → M_0, (α0,β0) ↦ (1-ρ_M)α0 - (1-σ_M)β0. Write α0 = a0λ0 + a1λ1 and β0 = b0λ0 + b1λ1. The kernel is given by c0 = a0 + a1 + (b1 - b0) = 0 and c1 = 2a1 - a0 - (b1 - b0) = 0.

Adding the two equations gives 3a1 = 0, so a1 = 0 over Z and then a0 = b0 - b1. Hence N^{0+} = {(b0-b1, 0, b0, b1)} is free of rank 2. The diagonal Z, n ↦ (nλ0, nλ0) (a1 = b1 = 0, a0 = b0), lies in it.

This page records the exact sequence (131): 0 → Z → N^{0+} → Γ^{0+} := N^{0+}/Z → 0, with Γ^{0+} free of rank 1 (coordinate b1). Hence (132): the group scheme Γ^{0+}_{ρ,σ} is isomorphic to the vector group of Γ^{0+}, i.e. G_a. He concludes that the group schemes just constructed (Γ_{ρ,σ}, an extension of O_12^* by Γ^{0+}_{ρ,σ}, relative dimension 2 noted in the margin) are smooth over Spec Z.

He then asks whether the extension N_{ρ,σ} of Γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0^M (sequence (127)) admits more or less natural sections. Given the 'équation des têtes' describing N_{ρ,σ}, such sections seem to come from choosing Z-module splittings of two sequences. These are 0 → N^{0+} (rank 2) → M⊕M → M_0 → 0 and (133) 0 → Z → N^{0+} → Γ^{0+} → 0. He cautions that one must check that these set-theoretic ('ensemblistes') sections of schemes allow one to define the multiplications. The thread is abandoned, and the next page passes to Z_{ρ,σ} and G_{ρ,σ}.
errors: The first map in (131) is written '1 →' although these are additive Z-modules; it should be 0 → Z (trivial slip).

The sequence 0 → N^{0+} → M⊕M → M_0 → 0 is written as if surjective onto M_0, but it is not. The image of (α0,β0) ↦ (1-ρ)α0 - (1-σ)β0 in M_0 ≅ Z^2 is spanned by (1,-1) and (1,2), which has index 3. The cokernel is Z/3, so this sequence is not exact on the right.

Consequently, if N^{0+}_{ρ,σ} is taken as the functorial (scheme-theoretic) kernel of W(M×M) → W(M_0), it is not flat over Spec Z. Mod 3 the two linear forms c0 = (1,1,-1,1) and c1 = (-1,2,1,-1) become proportional (c1 ≡ 2c0). So the fibre at p = 3 has dimension 3 rather than 2, and the smoothness claim fails at 3.

The claims (129) N^{0+}_{ρ,σ} ≃ W(N^{0+}) and smoothness over Spec Z therefore hold only if 'underline' means the vector group of the Z-module kernel, or after inverting 3. Grothendieck does not address this; the next page's condition (136) 'localement dans l'image de (1-ρ_M)' suggests image/torsion issues were on his mind.

ideas.what: Computing the Z-module kernel N^{0+} of (α,β) ↦ (1-ρ)α - (1-σ)β, and its quotient by the diagonal Z, as a free rank-1 module, giving a G_a factor
ideas.modern_name: Linear algebra of the abelianised (metabelian) action / Fox-calculus-type kernel; vector group scheme W(E)

ideas.what: Group schemes over Spec Z (extensions of O_12^* by vector groups) parametrising twisted conjugacy data (ξρ, ησ) for the generators of SL2(Z)/modular-type group, with an 'equation of heads'
ideas.modern_name: Integral (group-scheme) models of metabelian / affine approximations to Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type automorphism groups of the modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related ideas: Ihara (metabelian/power-series representations of GT-type actions), Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps for GT; integral group-scheme version unclear
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to themes of La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme; the specific construction is not known to be published

ideas.what: Question of natural sections of the extension N_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} with kernel L_0^M, obtained from Z-module splittings, and whether they respect group laws
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of group-scheme extensions / set-theoretic sections and cocycles

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether the extension of the smooth group scheme Γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0^M admits natural sections that are compatible with multiplication. He leaves this open, noting only that splittings of the underlying Z-module sequences give candidate set-theoretic sections. Behind it lies the unanswered question of whether these integral models of the twisted-conjugation automorphism groups split.
missed.quote: Peut-on définir des sections plus ou moins naturelles de l'extension N_{ρ,σ} de Γ_{ρ,σ} par L_0^M ... Mais il faut vérifier que les sections ... permettent de définir des multiplications
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor; it would interest only someone reconstructing integral or arithmetic models of GT-type actions on the modular group. The prime 3 (non-flatness) is a genuine subtlety in any such integral model.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine linear-algebra step inside an unpublished, idiosyncratic construction of group schemes over Z tied to the Longue Marche programme. The broader programme is mildly interesting, but this page contributes only a rank computation, a smoothness claim (which fails at p = 3 under the natural scheme-theoretic reading) and an open question about sections.
transcription_corrections: '1 → Z → N^{0+}' should read with 0 (Grothendieck himself wrote '1', but it means 0).
'21 déf [?] N^{0+}/Z' is 'Γ^{0+} ≝ N^{0+}/Z' (definition sign under Γ^{0+}).
'Ceci en conduit' is likely 'Ceci nous conduit' / 'On en conclut'.
'Ainsi, dans les schémas en groupes qu'on vient de construire sont lisses' should read 'Ainsi, les schémas en groupes qu'on vient de construire sont lisses sur Spec Z'.
'l'équation [?] des lecteurs [?]' is almost certainly 'l'équation des têtes' (cf. 'équation des têtes' on next page).
'lisse de dimension relative 2' is a marginal annotation under Γ_{ρ,σ}.
'des Z-modules). Mais il' plausibly reads '(scindages de Z-modules)'.
'sections "raisonnables" [?]' is more likely 'sections "ensemblistes"' (set-theoretic sections), with 'des schémas qui permettent de définir des multiplications'.
'il semble qu'on trouve des telles sections dès qu'on choisit un scindage des' continues with '...des suites exactes 0 → N^{0+} (rg 2) → M⊕M → M_0 → 0 et (133)'.
